macOS and Windows run the temp-HOME and temp-registry-key round trips in CI.

rows.summary: krate/theme.* reads the system appearance (light or dark, high contrast), reports changes and makes native title bars follow it or a fixed choice: the desktop portal and gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme on Linux, NSApp.appearance on macOS, the Personalize registry key and DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE on Windows.
knownLimits: Linux was tested against a fake portal and by reading back the GTK setting; whether a given desktop redraws its title bars is up to the window manager (client-side GTK decorations follow it).
macOS observes AppleInterfaceThemeChangedNotification, not KVO on effectiveAppearance.

rows.summary: A Go panic or fatal error in the shell or the Go host is written to a JSON report under the app's log directory (runtime/debug.SetCrashOutput, collected on the next launch), and a crashed or killed webview process is reported as an event and a report; krate/crash.* lists, reads and deletes reports, and can reload a crashed view automatically (at most three times in 30 seconds). WebKitGTK web-process-terminated, WKWebView webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate: and WebView2 ProcessFailed.
knownLimits: A crash of the shell itself is reported on the next launch, not live.
Nothing is uploaded; the app reads the reports and sends them where it likes.
WKWebView does not say why its process ended, so macOS reports the reason as crashed.

rows.area: Native: size, start-up and memory budgets
rows.summary: packages/native/budgets.json limits the stripped shell, Go-only, TypeScript-only and example release executables (bytes), the cold start of the example in a real window (ms) and its resident memory (KB). Limits are the measured value plus 25 percent. linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-arm64, windows-amd64 and windows-arm64 have entries; a platform with entries is enforced by the same measured-plus-headroom rule, one without only reports and prints a paste-ready BUDGET-RECORD block.
knownLimits: linux-amd64 was measured on a developer machine; linux-arm64, darwin-arm64, windows-amd64 and windows-arm64 were recorded from one green CI run on the GitHub-hosted runners, so they describe those runners rather than typical user machines.
CI multiplies every cold-start limit by 3 (KRATE_BUDGET_SCALE): hosted runners vary a lot in start-up time. Memory limits are not scaled; only appMinusFloor entries fail the job.
darwin-amd64 (Intel Macs) has no hosted runner in the CI matrix and no entries, so it only reports.

rows.area: Native: custom title bars, drag regions and transparency
rows.summary: native.window.titleBar hidden or none removes the system title bar; the page marks drag regions with data-krate-drag, -webkit-app-region or app-region (read from its style sheets, or by WebView2 itself) and a press starts the native move, a double press maximizes, and frameless windows keep resize edges (GTK draws them in the page, Windows hit-tests them, AppKit keeps its own). The window and webview can be transparent. The request that starts a move names no window: the shell finds it from the webview that sent it.
knownLimits: Linux: the drag and resize tests press a real pointer with XTEST under openbox on X11; Wayland compositors decide where a dragged window goes and are untested. Transparency needs an RGBA visual and, to show the desktop, a compositing window manager.

macOS and Windows: untested. The code compiles for them, the hit test, colors and style arithmetic are unit-tested on every OS, and GUI tests that read AppKit and Win32 state back run in the CI native job; nothing here has run on a Mac or a Windows PC by hand.

Windows draws the caption buttons of a hidden title bar itself, over the extended frame, so the page must leave that corner clear; the WebView2 non-client region support needs a recent runtime and falls back to the page script without it.
CSS regions are read from style sheets as text: nesting and @import are not followed, and the nearest marked ancestor wins rather than CSS specificity.

rows.area: Native: Mica, Acrylic, vibrancy, caption overlay and traffic lights
rows.summary: Windows 11 22H2 system backdrops (Mica, Mica Alt, Acrylic) behind a transparent webview, the caption buttons Windows draws over a hidden title bar with Snap Layouts on the maximize button (WM_NCHITTEST returns HTMAXBUTTON) and their colors, and on macOS an NSVisualEffectView with any current material behind a transparent WKWebView and a movable traffic light position. Calls the platform lacks reject with unsupported.
knownLimits: The WebView2 vtables for ICoreWebView2Controller2 and ICoreWebView2Settings9 are generated from WebView2.h and checked against it.
Backdrops need Windows 11 22H2 (build 22621); earlier builds reject them. A backdrop shows only where the page is transparent.
Vibrancy attaches the effect view to the window's frame view, below the content view, which AppKit allows but does not document.

rows.area: Native: tabs, sheets, document state, share menu, dock, thumbnail buttons and jump lists
rows.summary: macOS: document-edited and represented-file title bar state, windows as sheets, native window tabs with merge, move and new-tab events, the share picker for text, URLs and files, and menu-bar-only apps (activation policy at run time, LSUIElement in Info.plist from native.bundle.macos.agent, dock icon show and hide). Windows: taskbar thumbnail toolbar buttons with click events and jump list tasks that relaunch the app with arguments.
knownLimits: The macOS tab test skips when the CI session does not merge windows into tabs, and the share picker is validated but not shown in CI.

Thumbnail buttons need Explorer to create the taskbar button; without a shell session they stay pending. The jump list is committed through ICustomDestinationList and checked by its return codes, not by reading the shell's list back.
A new-tab event is delivered through the window delegate's newWindowForTab: action, the way AppKit sends it from the tab bar's plus button.

rows.summary: Background worker processes declared in native.workers (a TypeScript module on Node, Bun or Deno, a Go main package, or a prebuilt executable) are started by name from a page or host code, with their own SDK endpoint whose permissions are narrowed per worker, stdout and stderr in the app log, a restart policy with backoff, crash and restart events, and two-way messages over the wire codec (binary, Date, Map, Set). The supervisor and policy are pure Go and tested on every OS; the shell tests run real Node and Go workers.
knownLimits: macOS and Windows compile and share the portable supervisor and the host child transport (loopback TCP with a token for JavaScript workers on Windows); the worker tests and the procs end-to-end test run in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows.

A release build ships worker scripts under host/workers next to the executable and needs Node, Bun or Deno on the user's machine for a TypeScript worker; a Go worker is compiled for the build machine's platform only.
Permissions narrow the SDK ids a worker can call; a worker is still an ordinary process with the user's file and network access.

rows.area: Native: message ports between views, windows and workers
rows.summary: A channel has two ends; whoever creates it can hand each end to a window, view or worker, and messages (JSON, binary, Date, Map, Set) then flow directly between the ends without host code relaying them, in order, with a bounded queue (1024 messages, 16 MiB) and backpressure errors. An end can only be handed to a scope that has port:receive. The page object is a Port in @krate/app/port backed by the shell.
knownLimits: The engines give two top-level webviews no way to share a real MessagePort, so a port is a shell-backed object, not a transferable MessagePort; inside one page the browser's MessageChannel is untouched.
The pure broker is tested on every OS; the page-to-page and page-to-worker round trips run in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows.

rows.summary: No system webview streams offscreen frames. The closest equivalent: a window that is never shown (a GtkOffscreenWindow on Linux, a window parked off every display on Windows and macOS) whose page renders normally, plus snapshots (webkit_web_view_get_snapshot, WKWebView takeSnapshot, WebView2 CapturePreview) delivered as PNG or raw premultiplied BGRA, one at a time at a requested rate up to 60 per second, with dropped frames counted instead of queued.
knownLimits: This is polling, not a paint callback: frames are snapshots, so the rate depends on page complexity and engine; the measured Linux numbers are in docs native/processes.
Windows and macOS run the capture and parked-window code in the CI native job.
An open offscreen window counts as a window: close it, or the app does not quit when the last visible window closes.

rows.summary: An endpoint for tests and debugging, on in dev and with native.debug and never in a release build otherwise: WebView2 serves the Chrome DevTools Protocol (Playwright connectOverCDP, Puppeteer connect) and krate can send one CDP method or subscribe to an event in process; WebKitGTK serves the WebKit remote inspector over HTTP (WEBKIT_INSPECTOR_HTTP_SERVER), which is not CDP; WKWebView is inspectable from Safari's Develop menu. CDP answers unsupported where the engine does not speak it.
knownLimits: Playwright and Puppeteer attach only to WebView2; they cannot drive WebKitGTK or WKWebView. Microsoft documents --remote-debugging-port with Edge WebDriver's DebuggerAddress for WebView2; attaching Playwright through connectOverCDP to the same port is standard Chromium CDP but was not run here.
The WebView2 CDP command and event code is checked against WebView2.h and compiled; it runs only in the CI native job.

rows.summary: native.extensions packages unpacked extension folders loaded at start and by name: WebView2 through ICoreWebView2Profile7 AddBrowserExtension with AreBrowserExtensionsEnabled, WKWebView through WKWebExtensionController on macOS 15.4 and later. WebKitGTK has no extension API and answers unsupported.
knownLimits: Linux is unsupported by the engine.

WebView2 and macOS are written and compiled and never run by the author. On macOS the API's match patterns cover http, https and file pages, so a content script is not expected to run on the app's own krate:// pages.

rows.area: Native: accessibility of the shell's own UI
rows.summary: The UI the shell draws or configures is checked through each platform's accessibility API: window names in every title bar style, the webview reachable in native, hidden, frameless, transparent, split and remote windows, menus and context menus (roles, names, checked, disabled, accelerators), message and file dialogs, tray, notification, thumbnail button and jump list names, split-pane dividers, and offscreen windows kept out of the tree. Fixes: offscreen windows hidden (Linux AT-SPI, macOS AX), message dialog titles reach the accessible name, split panes and dividers named, tray and notification action and thumbnail button names never empty, Windows message box labels spelled out in the text, macOS alert default button, and drag regions no longer swallow presses on ARIA widgets and focusable elements.
knownLimits: Linux is checked through AT-SPI on X11 with a private accessibility bus and keys synthesized by at-spi2-registryd (needs the at-spi2-core package and a window manager); Wayland and a real screen reader were not used.

macOS is checked in process through NSAccessibility (no permission needed); the AX API tests skip unless the test process is trusted for accessibility, which CI runners are not. Runs in the CI native job.

Windows is checked through UI Automation; runs in the CI native job. The caption buttons of a hidden title bar are reported, not required; the notification area, taskbar thumbnails and jump lists are not read by tests (names come from unit-tested helpers).

Windows: split-pane dividers are mouse-only, frameless windows have no system menu, offscreen windows stay in the UI Automation tree marked offscreen, and a two-button message box cannot be closed with Esc.
macOS: an alert is dismissed with Esc only through a button titled Cancel; the split divider is reachable by VoiceOver but not by a plain keyboard.
No screen reader (Orca, VoiceOver, Narrator, NVDA, JAWS) was used on any platform; web content inside the webview is exposed by the engine and not tested here.

rows.summary: toast() and <Toaster /> render and show a toast with its description (sonner 2.0.8). Checked in Chromium by TestBrowserEcosystemLibraries against the real package (the test needs KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_LIBS or KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_INSTALL=1 and is skipped otherwise).
knownLimits: toast() and <Toaster /> must live in one island module: a component that only calls toast() is not detected as an island, so the build fails with "cannot bundle sonner for the browser" (react is not aliased to preact/compat in the page vendor bundle), and importing a helper from the island module leaves the binding undefined in the page.

The usual shadcn pattern (a <Toaster /> wrapper in the root layout, toast() called from other components) does not work yet: a layout cannot host the island (KR8013), and toast() in a separate component hits the first limit.

rows.summary: Command, Command.Input, Command.List, Command.Item and Command.Empty render, filter as you type and show the empty state (cmdk 1.1.1). Checked in Chromium by TestBrowserEcosystemLibraries against the real package (the test needs KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_LIBS or KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_INSTALL=1 and is skipped otherwise).

useEmblaCarousel initializes on mount, reports its snap list and scrolls on api.scrollNext() (embla-carousel-react 8.6.0). Checked in Chromium by TestBrowserEcosystemLibraries against the real package (the test needs KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_LIBS or KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_INSTALL=1 and is skipped otherwise).

DndContext, SortableContext and useSortable with the pointer sensor reorder a list through a real drag (@dnd-kit/core 6.3.1, @dnd-kit/sortable 10.0.0, @dnd-kit/utilities 3.2.2). Checked in Chromium by TestBrowserEcosystemLibraries against the real package (the test needs KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_LIBS or KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_INSTALL=1 and is skipped otherwise).

useReactTable with the core and sorted row models, column helpers and flexRender render the table on the server and re-sort on a header click (8.21.3). The v9 API (react-table 9) was not checked. Checked in Chromium by TestBrowserEcosystemLibraries against the real package (the test needs KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_LIBS or KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_INSTALL=1 and is skipped otherwise).

ThemeProvider and useTheme switch the class on <html> and update the theme state; the anti-flash script is part of the server markup (next-themes 0.4.6). Checked in Chromium by TestBrowserEcosystemLibraries against the real package (the test needs KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_LIBS or KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_INSTALL=1 and is skipped otherwise).
knownLimits: A ThemeProvider in a layout is not lifted into the islands (KR8016: it renders a script next to its children), so useTheme in pages and components outside the provider's own module sees no context. Wrap the island's module in the provider instead.
The server markup renders the theme as undefined until the island hydrates, as it does with React.

rows.summary: motion.div with initial/animate/transition, and AnimatePresence with an exit animation, run and unmount their element (motion 14.14.0, imported from motion/react). The older framer-motion package and the vanilla Motion engine config key are separate rows. Checked in Chromium by TestBrowserEcosystemLibraries against the real package (the test needs KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_LIBS or KRATE_ECOSYSTEM_INSTALL=1 and is skipped otherwise).
knownLimits: Building a page that imports motion/react logs the warning KR7116 (two motion-dom modules export scrapeMotionValuesFromProps); it does not affect the result.
